# 什么是 ClaudeBot？

- 原标题：What Is ClaudeBot?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/claudebot/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

ClaudeBot 是 Anthropic 运行的网络爬虫，用于收集公开网页内容，训练其 Claude AI 模型。它在服务器日志中使用“ClaudeBot”这一 User-Agent 标识，遵守 robots.txt 中的禁止访问指令，也是 Anthropic 多种机器人之一，其他还包括 Claude-User 和 Claude-SearchBot。

### 核心要点

- User-Agent 标识为 `ClaudeBot`，完整自我标识字符串为 `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0; +claudebot@anthropic.com)`。
- Anthropic 运行多种不同机器人：用于模型训练的 ClaudeBot、用于用户发起访问的 Claude-User，以及用于搜索索引的 Claude-SearchBot。它们各有独立标识，需要在 robots.txt 中分别设置。
- Anthropic 表示，其机器人尊重 robots.txt。要屏蔽训练抓取，需要先写 `User-agent: ClaudeBot`，再写 `Disallow: /`。
- 2024 年 7 月，iFixit 报告 ClaudeBot 在 24 小时内访问其服务器约一百万次，使抓取速率，而不仅仅是是否同意抓取，成为发布者面临的现实问题。

### ClaudeBot 如何运作

ClaudeBot 是 Anthropic 在不断增加的 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)群体中的一员。这些自动代理会下载公开网页，让公司能够为模型构建训练数据。从功能上看，它与任何遵守规范的搜索爬虫类似：通过 HTTP 请求网页，在 `User-Agent` 请求头中标识自己，并遵循机器人排除协议。区别在用途：Googlebot 抓取是为了建立搜索索引，ClaudeBot 抓取则是为了帮助训练 Anthropic 的 Claude 语言模型系列。

它使用的标识就是 `ClaudeBot`，完整 User-Agent 字符串里还包含联系地址：`Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0; +claudebot@anthropic.com)`。网站所有者可以据此在服务器日志中识别它，并针对该标识决定是否放行。Anthropic 会公布机器人抓取所用的 IP 范围，让运营者核验一个自称 ClaudeBot 的请求，确实来自 Anthropic，而不是伪造这个字符串的冒充者。

关键是，ClaudeBot 不是 Anthropic 唯一运行的机器人。把“ClaudeBot”当成“Anthropic”的同义词，正是大多数屏蔽错误的起点。

### Anthropic 的机器人

Anthropic 的官方文档将网页访问划分给不同的 User-Agent，每一种都有明确职责和独立的 robots.txt 标识：

- **ClaudeBot**：广泛抓取公开内容，用于模型训练和开发。
- **Claude-User**：按需获取页面。当 Claude 用户提出的问题需要实时网页内容时，这个标识会提取回答所需的具体页面。
- **Claude-SearchBot**：索引机器人，收集内容以改善 Claude 展示的搜索结果质量。

因为标识彼此独立，禁止 `ClaudeBot` 的规则不会影响另外两种。希望完全退出的网站所有者，需要为每个机器人分别写规则。这与 OpenAI 的 [GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/) 和 [OAI-SearchBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/oai-searchbot/)之间的逐机器人控制逻辑相同，也解释了为什么认真制定的 [AI 机器人屏蔽](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/)政策是一份标识列表，而不是单独一行。有些发布者还会在 [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) 文件中声明抓取偏好，作为补充信号。

### ClaudeBot 示例

展示 ClaudeBot 现实影响的最清楚记录，是 **2024 年 7 月**的 iFixit 事件。据 404 Media 报道，iFixit 首席执行官 Kyle Wiens 表示，ClaudeBot 在 **24 小时内约一百万次**访问这家维修网站的服务器，消耗了运维资源，并以让 Wiens 在社交媒体上公开反对的速度抓取内容。

解决过程最有启发性。iFixit 原本有宽泛的抓取延迟和禁止访问政策，却没有点名 Anthropic 的具体标识。网站增加明确的 `User-agent: ClaudeBot` 禁止规则后，Anthropic 确认爬虫尊重了这一信号，并停止访问。机器人本身没有改变，它一直遵守 robots.txt，只是只遵守发给*自身*标识的指令。这件事同时说明了两点：AI 爬虫可以带来真实的基础设施负载；退出抓取也必须针对具体标识。一个没有提到 `ClaudeBot` 的泛化反抓取规则，阻止不了 ClaudeBot。

### 人们常犯的错误

我经常看到团队在 robots.txt 里加入“User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /”，就以为已经让自己的内容与 Claude 完全隔绝，事实并非如此。这条规则只停止*训练*爬虫，对 Claude-User 没有作用。后者是 Anthropic 在真实 Claude 用户提出需要获取网页的问题时所用的独立标识：不同机器人、不同用途，需要 robots.txt 中另一条规则。如果目标是“不用我的内容训练”，屏蔽 ClaudeBot 是正确做法。如果目标是“任何 Anthropic 系统都不能访问我的页面”，一条规则不够，必须逐个点名。看清标识，而不只是厂商名称。

### 常见问题

#### ClaudeBot 是什么？

ClaudeBot 是 Anthropic 的网络爬虫，会系统性下载公开网页，为其 Claude AI 模型系列构建训练数据。它使用“ClaudeBot”这一 User-Agent 标识，并遵守 robots.txt 中禁止它访问的规则。

#### 如何屏蔽 ClaudeBot？

在 robots.txt 中添加两行：先写 `User-agent: ClaudeBot`，再写 `Disallow: /`。Anthropic 表示 ClaudeBot 会遵守该指令。如需同时阻止其他 Anthropic 机器人，还要为 Claude-User 和 Claude-SearchBot 分别添加规则，因为它们各用不同标识。

#### 屏蔽 ClaudeBot 会让我的网站从 Claude 中消失吗？

不会。屏蔽 ClaudeBot 只停止未来的训练抓取，不会删除已经学到的内容，也不会阻止 Claude-User。后者是 Anthropic 在用户问题需要时，实时获取网页的独立标识。

#### ClaudeBot 和 Claude-User 相同吗？

不同。ClaudeBot 广泛抓取网络，以收集训练数据；Claude-User 则在 Claude 用户提出需要实时网页内容的问题时，按需获取特定页面。它们具有不同的 User-Agent 标识与用途，在 robots.txt 中分别控制。

### 要点总结

ClaudeBot 是 Anthropic 的训练数据爬虫，是读取公开页面以训练 Claude 的自动代理。它只是 Anthropic 机器人家族中的一员；明确点名其标识时，它会遵守 robots.txt。控制它是一项逐标识的工作：屏蔽 ClaudeBot 可拒绝训练抓取，但如果也想管理实时访问和搜索访问，就要分别处理 Claude-User 和 Claude-SearchBot。

## 英文原文

ClaudeBot is the web crawler Anthropic operates to collect public web content for training its Claude AI models. It identifies itself in server logs with the user-agent token “ClaudeBot,” honors robots.txt disallow directives, and is one of several Anthropic bots alongside Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot.

### Key Takeaways

- The user-agent token is `ClaudeBot`; it self-identifies with the string `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0; +claudebot@anthropic.com)`.
- Anthropic runs several distinct bots — ClaudeBot (model training), Claude-User (user-initiated fetches), and Claude-SearchBot (search indexing) — each a separate token you address individually in robots.txt.
- Anthropic states its bots respect robots.txt; blocking training crawls requires `User-agent: ClaudeBot` followed by `Disallow: /`.
- In July 2024, iFixit reported ClaudeBot hit its servers roughly one million times in 24 hours, making crawl rate — not just consent — a live concern for publishers.

### How ClaudeBot Works

ClaudeBot is Anthropic’s contribution to the growing population of [AI crawlers](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) — automated agents that download public web pages so a company can build training data for its models. Functionally it behaves like any well-mannered search crawler: it requests pages over HTTP, identifies itself in the `User-Agent` header, and follows the Robots Exclusion Protocol. The difference is intent. Where Googlebot crawls to build a search index, ClaudeBot crawls to help teach Claude, Anthropic’s family of language models.

The token it presents is simply `ClaudeBot`, and its full user-agent string embeds a contact address: `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0; +claudebot@anthropic.com)`. That self-identification is what lets a site owner recognize it in server logs and decide, per token, whether to allow it. Anthropic publishes the IP ranges its bots crawl from so operators can verify that a request claiming to be ClaudeBot genuinely originates from Anthropic rather than an impostor spoofing the string.

Crucially, ClaudeBot is not the only bot Anthropic runs, and treating “ClaudeBot” as a synonym for “Anthropic” is where most blocking mistakes begin.

### Anthropic’s Bots

Anthropic’s own documentation splits its web access into distinct user agents, each with a narrow job and its own robots.txt token:

- **ClaudeBot** — the broad crawler that collects public content for model training and development.
- **Claude-User** — the on-demand fetcher. When a Claude user asks something that needs live web content, this token retrieves the specific pages required to answer.
- **Claude-SearchBot** — the indexer that gathers content to improve the quality of search results Claude surfaces.

Because each is a separate token, a rule that disallows `ClaudeBot` leaves the other two untouched. Site owners who want a complete opt-out have to write a block for each. This is the same per-bot logic that governs [GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/) versus [OAI-SearchBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/oai-searchbot/) on the OpenAI side, and it is why a serious [AI bot blocking](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/) policy is a list of tokens, not a single line. Some publishers also declare their crawl preferences in an [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) file as a complementary signal.

### Example of ClaudeBot

The clearest documented illustration of ClaudeBot’s real-world impact is the iFixit incident of **July 2024**. As reported by 404 Media, iFixit CEO Kyle Wiens said ClaudeBot had hit the repair site’s servers roughly **one million times in a 24-hour window**, consuming devops resources and pulling content at a pace Wiens publicly objected to on social media.

The resolution is the instructive part. iFixit had a broad crawl-delay and disallow policy but had not named Anthropic’s specific token. Once the site added an explicit `User-agent: ClaudeBot` disallow rule, Anthropic confirmed the crawler respected that signal and stopped. Nothing about the bot changed — it honored robots.txt the whole time — but it only honored the directive addressed to *its* token. The episode became a reference point for two lessons at once: that AI crawlers can generate real infrastructure load, and that opting out is token-specific. A generic anti-scraping rule that never mentions `ClaudeBot` will not stop ClaudeBot.

### The thing people get wrong

The mistake I see constantly is a team adding "User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /" to robots.txt and assuming they’ve walled their content off from Claude entirely. They haven’t. That rule stops the *training* crawler. It does nothing about Claude-User, the separate token Anthropic uses when a live Claude user asks a question that requires fetching a page — a different bot, a different purpose, a different line in your robots.txt. If your goal is "don’t train on my content," blocking ClaudeBot is the right move. If your goal is "no Anthropic system ever touches my pages," one line won’t do it; you have to name each bot. Read the token, not the vendor.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is ClaudeBot?

ClaudeBot is Anthropic’s web crawler. It systematically downloads public web pages to build training data for Claude, Anthropic’s family of AI models. It announces itself with the user-agent token “ClaudeBot” and honors robots.txt rules that disallow it.

#### How do I block ClaudeBot?

Add two lines to your robots.txt: `User-agent: ClaudeBot` then `Disallow: /`. Anthropic states ClaudeBot honors this directive. To stop other Anthropic bots too, add separate blocks for Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot, since each uses its own token.

#### Does blocking ClaudeBot remove my site from Claude?

No. Blocking ClaudeBot only stops future training crawls. It does not delete content already learned, and it does not stop Claude-User — the separate token Anthropic uses to fetch a page in real time when a user’s question requires it.

#### Is ClaudeBot the same as Claude-User?

No. ClaudeBot crawls the web broadly to gather training data. Claude-User fetches specific pages on demand when a Claude user asks something that needs live web content. They are distinct user-agent tokens with different purposes and are controlled separately in robots.txt.

### The Bottom Line

ClaudeBot is Anthropic’s training-data crawler — the automated agent that reads public pages to teach Claude. It is only one member of Anthropic’s bot family, it obeys robots.txt when you name its token, and controlling it is a per-token exercise: block ClaudeBot to opt out of training, but address Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot separately if you want to govern real-time and search access too.
